title: Core scalar Cech external cup compatibility
statement: Let k be a field, X and Y schemes over k, F and G quasi-coherent modules, U and V open covers (iSup U = top and iSup V = top), and c a cochain map satisfying [lem-sc-picard-external-cech-cup-component]. Let eX, eY and eP be degreewise scalar comparisons satisfying [lem-sc-picard-scalar-cech-comparison]. For p+q=n and factor cycles a,b and a total cycle z whose inclusion is the (p,q)-summand tensor of the factor cycle inclusions, eP(H(c)([z])) is externalCup of eX([a]) and eY([b]), transported along p+q=n.

proof.text: Eliminate the degree equality p+q=n. Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.homologyπ_naturality to replace H(c)([z]) by the class of cyclesMap c z. Apply HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i, the assumed cycle-inclusion equality, and the IsPicardExternalCechCupComponent coordinate formula to identify every tuple coordinate of this image cycle with the external front/back tensor. Apply the external cocycle comparison to that cycle and the degreewise comparison maps. The reflexive degree cast disappears.

proof_origin.place: G3: separate the explicit cochain-to-cycle calculation from the resolution comparison, Tags 01FD, 07MB, 0FKV and 0BED.

lean.statement:
theorem picardScalarCech_externalCup_core
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    {ι κ : Type w} (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : κ → Y.Opens)
    (hUc : iSup U = ⊤) (hVc : iSup V = ⊤)
    (c : HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor ((picardCechFunctor f U).obj F)
        ((picardCechFunctor g V).obj G) (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ) ⟶
      (picardCechFunctor (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
        (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
          pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2)).obj (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))
    (hc : IsPicardExternalCechCupComponent f g U V F G c)
    (eX : ∀ p : ℕ, ((picardCechFunctor f U).obj F).homology p →ₗ[k]
      scalarCohomology f F p)
    (heX : ∀ p, IsPicardScalarCechComparison f U F p (eX p))
    (eY : ∀ q : ℕ, ((picardCechFunctor g V).obj G).homology q →ₗ[k]
      scalarCohomology g G q)
    (heY : ∀ q, IsPicardScalarCechComparison g V G q (eY q))
    (eP : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((picardCechFunctor (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
        (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
          pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2)).obj
            (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)).homology n →ₗ[k]
        scalarCohomology (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) n)
    (heP : ∀ n, IsPicardScalarCechComparison (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
      (fun ij : ι × κ ↦ pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U ij.1 ⊓
        pullback.snd f g ⁻¹ᵁ V ij.2) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) n (eP n)) :
    let A := (picardCechFunctor f U).obj F
    let B := (picardCechFunctor g V).obj G
    let T := HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor A B (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : {pq : ℕ × ℕ // pq.1 + pq.2 = n})
    (a : A.cycles i.val.1) (v : B.cycles i.val.2) (z : T.cycles n),
    T.iCycles n z = HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor A B
        (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k)) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) i.val.1 i.val.2 n
        i.property ((A.iCycles i.val.1 a) ⊗ₜ[k] (B.iCycles i.val.2 v)) →
      eP n (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c n (T.homologyπ n z)) =
        cast (congrArg (fun d ↦ ↥(scalarCohomology (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
          (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) d)) i.property)
          (externalCup f g F G i.val.1 i.val.2
            (eX i.val.1 (A.homologyπ _ a)) (eY i.val.2 (B.homologyπ _ v)))

statement_change.old_statement: Under the coefficient and comparison hypotheses of lem-sc-picard-scalar-cech-external-cup, without the cover equalities, the displayed cycle compatibility formula holds.
statement_change.what:
The old cover-free helper is false. Take X=Y=P¹ over a field k with two
rational points x₀ and x₁, U=V={P¹ \ {x₁}}, and F=G the direct sum of the two
skyscraper modules k(x₀) and k(x₁). These modules are quasi-coherent. Since
Γ(P¹,O)=k and Γ(P¹×P¹,O)=k, the comparisons in degree zero need only be
k-linear, even though IsModuleCechComparison requires global-ring linearity.
The singleton Cech H⁰ is k and global H⁰ is k². The factor comparisons can
send s to (s,0), and the product comparison can send s to (s,s,s,s) in k⁴.
They satisfy IsModuleCechComparison: the alpha/beta equation is restriction
to the chosen open, which discards the omitted skyscraper summands. More
explicitly, sections on that open are exact on these finite-support modules,
so the resolution total computes the restricted module's H⁰=k; the equation
holds for every resolution. All higher factor and product Cech groups vanish,
so take the zero comparisons in higher degrees. The standard front/back
cochain pairing supplies c and hc. For a=b=1 its product comparison is
(1,1,1,1), while externalCup of the factor comparisons is (1,0,0,0).
The original Spec(k×k) example was invalid: its global-ring idempotents force
an O(X)-linear comparison to vanish on omitted components.
Tags 01FD and 0FKV assume open coverings. Restore the enclosing theorem's
exact cover hypotheses to this helper; no target or enclosing theorem changes.

old_proof.text: Fix the displayed degree, summand, cycles and total cycle. Expand the refinement and Alexander–Whitney coordinates and use the comparison witnesses; scalar restriction identifies the resulting cup with externalCup.
